text:
maya: Thinking about the rollout console fallback UX — we need to decide which degrade triggers are shown prominently vs buried in logs. currently it's a long list and people can't tell what actually caused the switch. :thinking:

sam: yep. my 2c: surface only the top 3 signals by impact and link to full telemetry. otherwise PMs get alarmed by noise.

juan: agree. also we should separate hard errors (500s, OOM) from soft signals (latency spike, error rate drift) in the UI. hard errors = immediate visible red banner.

lisa: can we compute a single "fallback score" that weights severity, velocity, and affected qps? then show the score + contributing signals.

kevin: hard question: how do we compute weights? heuristic first, allow overrides per-customer rollout policy. Ops needs to be able to tune without shipping code.

maya: yes — default weights in product, editable in rollout spec. UI should show which weights were used for that decision. auditability is critical.

ops-bot: [alert] fallback triggered for rollout r-104 at 2237708200 due to combined score 0.87 (latency=0.6, error-rate=0.2, kvcache-miss=0.07).

sam: ops-bot example is helpful. proposal: in the console event feed show a condensed line like that + a "why" panel with the raw signals and a sparkline for each.

juan: +1. And in the "why" panel we should include the fallback routing decision tree path that was taken (e.g., route->variant-b->region-fallback) so SREs can replay.

lisa: replayability note: the system needs to record model-variant ids, pinned versions, and runtime kernel profile at decision time, otherwise reenacting the scenario is useless.

kevin: Also need to enforce quota-aware fallbacks: if fallback routes to cheaper model but that model is out of quota for the tenant, it must skip that route and try next. UI should mark routes as "unavailable by quota" with tooltip.

maya: good call. The rollout policy editor should show the candidate route list and mark incompatible ones with reasons (quota, region, capability).

sam: telemetry requirements: for each fallback event we need timestamp, score breakdown, request sample rate, affected customers (sampled), and pre/post latency/cost deltas. This feeds alerts and regressions.

juan: and histograms for response time before/after fallback (p50/p90/p99) — UI should show delta and whether it met SLOs.

lisa: edge case: oscillation — fallback->recovery->fallback thrash. We should include a cooldown window in the decision trace and record how many times it oscillated in last X minutes. show that in the audit entry.

kevin: implementation note: decision evaluation must be idempotent and fully reproducible from the recorded inputs to satisfy compliance audits. Record random seeds, sampling flags, and model selection tie-breakers.

maya: UX for operators: make a compact "timeline" view for a rollout with events: triggers (collapsed), actions (expanded), and a checkbox to expand raw logs. copying runbook links and passthrough commands should be one click.

sam: on the policy schema side, add fields: signal_weights (map), signal_thresholds (map), cooldown_secs (int), max_oscillations (int). keep it JSON-editable in advanced, but provide wizards.

juan: example snippet we can show in console help: 
```
fallback_policy:
  signals:
    latency_ms:
      weight: 0.6
      threshold: 250
    error_rate:
      weight: 0.3
      threshold: 0.02
  cooldown_secs: 300
  max_oscillations: 2
```

lisa: +1. Also add a "simulator" in the rollout page where you can toggle a signal spike and preview which route would be chosen and what the audit entry looks like. Helps PM/ops trust defaults.

kevin: telemetry ingestion costs — we should sample signals aggressively for heavy tenants and keep aggregated counters for long-term. But for audits we need at least one full sample stored per fallback event.

maya: agreed. store a compressed snapshot for each fallback (one per event) + aggregated metrics for dashboards.

ops-bot: [info] logged fallback snapshot s-908 at 2237708301 (stored, compressed).

sam: final UX ask: make the fallback audit view exportable (CSV/JSON) with the decision tree, weights, and the pre/post metrics so infra teams can run offline analyses.

maya: ok next steps: sam to draft UI mockups for condensed event line + expand panel by EOD Friday. kevin to spec schema changes and minimal required fields. juan to draft decision replay requirements. lisa to draft sampling/retention policy for snapshots. I'll consolidate and we can review Wed sync. :thumbsup:

sam: on it.

kevin: starting schema doc now.

juan: I'll add replay acceptance criteria to the doc.

lisa: will write retention and cost tradeoffs.

maya: thanks everyone. leaving this in "needs mocks" until we have wireframes.
